finding: Overflow detection was VERTICAL-ONLY while the collapsed class hid BOTH axes and the description had no break-words: a hostile server could put its payload in one unbroken token, rendering a single line that never overflows vertically -> no toggle, remainder clipped horizontally with no cue. The exact hide-from-reviewer capability the change claims to close.

`if (beforeResult.silent) return` applied to ALL callers, not just the composer. The approval card transmits Approve/Deny via `chat.sendMessage()` with an EMPTY composer, relying on mcp's `discardCancel:['text']`; the registry swallows a throwing extension hook, so any failure of that discard downgraded a dropped CONSENT DECISION into a silent success. Previously it threw and the card reverted to pending_approval.

INV-4 violation with state damage: `startRegenerateMessage` latches pendingBranch fields and awaits `trimMessagesToForkPoint` BEFORE calling sendMessage. With an unconditional silent return (attachment-only preceding message => empty text), the transcript stays trimmed, nothing regenerates, no error is shown, and the latched fields make the user's NEXT send fork from a stale message.

INV-1 violation: the Send BUTTON is not disabled on an empty composer, so making the veto unconditionally silent turned a deliberate click into a dead click with no request, no toast and no disabled affordance. Previously it produced an explanatory toast.

A Vitest-authored test file committed INSIDE the chat store's actions/ dir is picked up by `index.ts`'s runtime `import.meta.glob('./actions/*.ts')` and registered as a lazy store action; store-kit's autoWarmLazyActions then preloads it, producing a failed dynamic import / `m.default is not a function` as an UNHANDLED rejection in the browser -- the very pageerror class this feature removes -- and drags vitest into a production chunk. `check:store-actions` does NOT catch it (the generator filters .test.ts).

`ApprovalToolDescription` re-implemented `chat/components/CollapsibleBlock.tsx` (same clamp, same ResizeObserver measurement, same Show more/less) while dropping three things the sibling encodes: `aria-controls`, the bottom fade mask that CUES hidden content, and the focus auto-expand for WCAG 2.4.7/2.4.11. CollapsibleBlock already accepts `maxHeightPx` and works without a messageId.

The new role=status/aria-live region was MOUNTED together with its content, contradicting the sibling 12 lines above whose comment states the live region is ALWAYS mounted (only its spinner content toggles) precisely so screen readers announce it. A region inserted with its content is unreliably announced.
aria-label sat on a lucide <svg> with no role=img, so the status region could compute an EMPTY accessible name and announce nothing.

The indicator renders for `(loading || isStreaming)` where `loading` is the message-history FETCH state, so a plain page load was announced as 'Generating response' and matched a testid named for streaming.
The toggle carried aria-expanded but no aria-controls, and the region had no id -- assistive tech could not associate the disclosure with what it governs.

A hard overflow-hidden edge with no fade cue: on a consent surface, 'looks like the description just ended' is the failure mode that matters. The sibling masks the clipped edge for exactly this reason.
Render condition `(overflowing || expanded)` could unmount the toggle while it held focus, dropping focus to <body> on a consent surface.

Expand/collapse changes row height inside the VIRTUALIZED MessageList with no scroll anchoring, so the viewport jumps and neighbours re-measure. The sibling routes the identical toggle through `useInPlaceAnchor` to prevent this.

The ResizeObserver was re-created on every toggle (`expanded` in the dep array) and observed the element whose height is PINNED by the clamp, so content-growth reflows could not fire it. setState-from-an-RO-callback is also the usual source of the 'ResizeObserver loop' console error the runtime-health gate treats as HIGH.

`expanded` was component-local state while the card remounts (loadMessages replaces the messages Map; the virtualizer unmounts off-screen rows), so a reviewer mid-read of a long attacker-supplied description silently lost the expansion.

The guard read render-closure values while `sending` is only set AFTER beforeSendMessage/composeRequestFields/(new chat) a createConversation round-trip, so two rapid Enters both observed false and both proceeded -- on a new chat that creates TWO conversations. The guard closed only the mid-stream case, not the repeat-keypress window it was documented to fix.
The comment claimed 'Mirror ChatInput.handleSend exactly' but omitted `disabled` and `isBlockedByExtension` -- an overclaiming comment future readers would trust.

`mergeBeforeSendResults` has NO production caller anywhere (definition + barrel re-export only). Routing it through a new `mergeCancelDecision` export added public API and unit tests purely to keep dead code in sync, and silently narrowed its return shape (errorMessage dropped on the no-cancel branch).

TEST-10b asserted only that the buttons sit above the fold. The message list auto-scrolls to its tail, so an UNCLAMPED card still ends with its footer in view -- it pushes its own HEADER off the top instead. Verified empirically: unclamped the card is 837px tall at y=-235; clamped 457px at y=145. The assertion could not distinguish clamped from scrolled-into-view and passed with the fix reverted.
TEST-7 injects its failure by 500-ing the send POST, which was ALREADY inside the pre-existing try/catch, so it cannot detect a revert of the try-widening it is billed as covering.

The test titled '...surfaces a toast' asserts the conversation error Alert, not the handler's toast. `sendMessage` swallows send failures and never rethrows, so the new TextInput catch is not exercised by it and its pageErrors assertion is trivially true.

consoleErrors was asserted empty over the WHOLE page lifetime (listener attached before login), so unrelated boot/auth/SSE noise would fail a composer spec -- flaky by construction, and 'fixed' by widening the ignore regex until the gate stops gating.

Three tests all derived from one fact -- that string literals appear in gallery.tsx SOURCE TEXT. None could fail if the clamp regressed, and they break on a formatter quote/spacing change. Coverage inflation over a formatting-coupled assertion.
Every assertion was on pure helpers with nothing binding them to the component; the component could stop calling them and all tests stay green.
`stubRegistry` assigns OWN properties shadowing the class prototype; afterEach 'restored' by re-assigning the prototype methods as own properties, so the shadowing was permanent rather than undone.

The abort branch awaits `loadMessages` unguarded inside the catch; a refetch failure would reject sendMessage even though the original failure was fully handled, surfacing a spurious toast for a user-initiated cancel.

With the silent path skipping both the registry log and the store's read of errorMessage, 'Message cannot be empty' became entirely dead -- an empty submit produced zero diagnostic trace despite the comment claiming it was kept for diagnostics.
'Failed to send message' hardcoded here while the same change introduced SEND_FAILED_FALLBACK_MESSAGE for exactly that string -- two copies of one user-facing string that can drift.

Behaviour change worth documenting: the old loop returned the FIRST non-discarded cancel in registration order; resolveCancel returns the first LOUD one. When text (silent) and file (loud) veto together the surfaced message changes from 'Message cannot be empty' to 'Please wait for files to finish uploading'. Intended (fail-loud-wins) but undocumented in the JSDoc.

`beforeSendMessage` catches a throwing extension hook, logs it, and records NO result -- an extension that crashes is treated as having APPROVED the send (fails open). Pre-existing, adjacent to the aggregation this change rewrites.

The catch writes failure state after awaiting onStreamError without re-validating the conversation; if the pane rebound mid-await the alert lands on the wrong conversation. Pre-existing shape (the catch already awaited before writing); the change adds one more awaited hop.

Pane asymmetry: the guard reads THIS pane's flags while the text extension reads the FOCUSED pane's TextStore. Pre-existing on the content side; the new guard makes the halves visibly inconsistent rather than uniformly focused-pane.
New strings are hardcoded English while i18next is a declared dependency. No useTranslation exists anywhere in src/ today, so this matches the codebase rather than regressing it.

The regenerated matrix carries line-number churn for surfaces this change does not touch, i.e. the committed artifact was already stale on the base branch and this change absorbs that drift. Real, but not attributable to this feature.
Assessed SAFE: toHaveText on approval-tool-description reads textContent (useInnerText off) and the clamp is CSS-only with the complete string rendered, so the existing disclosure spec still passes.

Assessed SAFE: every existing getByRole('status') assertion is either .first() on a non-chat page or scoped to inline-file-preview; no aria-snapshot tests exist. Adding role=status to the message list does not break them.
Positive trace: the silent flag IS wired end-to-end -- text extension -> registry resolveCancel -> store early return. Hop-by-hop confirmed by an independent reviewer.
